title: Sales Surgeon: Fallback Protocol and Rapid Triage Playbook (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight sales enablement deck + battlecard sketch for fast-moving seller and SE teams to triage and recover pilots or production incidents where inference economics or latency degrades. Tone: tactical, executable, and script-first (what to say, what to flip, who to call). Not final — intended as a one-pager + 8-slide speaker deck for 10-minute briefings and a short handoff checklist for platform/SRE.

Audience:
- Field sellers and SEs running pilot or early-production conversations
- Solutions engineers leading technical on-ramps
- Ops / SRE / Platform engineers receiving incident handoffs

One-line summary for sellers:
"If inference turns into a showstopper, follow this 6-step protocol to stabilize user experience within 10 minutes and preserve contract momentum."

Quick executive elevator note (for AE/SE):
- When latency/cost or quality variability threatens a pilot, prioritize user-facing stability -> then cost. Avoid reactive model swaps that change semantics without notice. Follow the protocol below to minimize churn and time-to-repair.

Deck outline (8 slides, speaker notes):
1) Title + Intent
- Speaker note: 30s framing: this is your fast map when inference degrades. Focus: keep users happy, preserve business metrics, reduce mean time to stabilization.

2) When to use this (triggers)
- Trigger examples: sustained P95 latency > 3s for interactive features, request queue growth > 25% of configured pool, unexpected token cost spike > 40% week-over-week, model hallucination/regression on top-10 prompts.
- Speaker note: call out thresholds we agreed with SRE. Use conservatively.

3) The 6-step Sales Surgeon Protocol (overview)
- 0) Calm script for customer (first 90s)
- 1) Quick triage (isolate route, check SLOs, capture logs)
- 2) Fast mitigation (route policy change: degrade by latency tier or pin to cached variant)
- 3) Temporary denoising (prompt compression, stop streaming)
- 4) Cost stopgap (apply rate limits or token caps for pilot)
- 5) Handoff packet to platform (collected logs + recommended rollback)
- Speaker note: each step should be <2 minutes except handoff.

4) What to say to the customer (canned lines)
- "We’ve detected an elevated response time for a subset of requests. I’m going to take a short protective action to make sure the experience stays fast for you while our ops team stabilizes things."
- "You may notice slightly more concise answers for a few minutes — this is an intentional mitigation to keep latency low."
- Speaker note: keep it honest, minimize technical jargon; emphasize temporary action and follow-up plan.

5) Rapid triage checklist (SE view)
- A. Identify impacted route(s): route id, model id, region, user token samples
- B. Metrics to snapshot: P50/P95 latency, queue length, GPU utilization, token-per-request, error rate (5 min window)
- C. Quick log captures: last 200 request ids and corresponding trace ids
- D. Routing policy check: has a new deployment or policy change rolled out in last 15m?
- E. External factors: cloud region availability, scheduled maintenance alerts
- Speaker note: these can be copy/pasted into Slack message to SRE.

6) Fast mitigations (actions you can perform now)
- Action 1: Route to lower-cost/latency-compatible variant (e.g., -quantized or lower context window) and keep same API surface. Latency improvement: typical 30–60% reduction.
- Action 2: Enable prefix/KV cache for repetitive prompts (if not enabled) — immediate win for chatbots.
- Action 3: Apply a per-customer token cap or reduce max_tokens on generation calls to reduce tail latency.
- Action 4: Temporarily disable streaming to reduce connection overhead if streaming jitter observed.
- Action 5: Toggle autoscale burst off/on per the pilot contract to free reserved capacity for higher-priority traffic.
- Speaker note: include exact console paths or API calls in the final doc. For now, high-level.

7) Hand-off packet for Platform/SRE (what to include)
- Minimum packet: incident id, time window, route ids, model variants, last change id (deployment or policy), metric snapshots (P95/P99), example request+response pairs, traces (trace ids), screenshot of console model timeline.
- Recommended immediate ops steps: rollback last deployment, pin policy to previous stable routing, increase pool priority for this customer if SLA covers it.

8) Post-mortem & owner communications
- Required within 48 hours for any production-impacting event: short incident summary, impact metric (user-facing sessions affected), root cause hypothesis, and a mitigation plan with owners and dates.
- Speaker note: align PM + Account owner on next customer-facing comms.

Battlecard quick reference (1-page):
- Symptoms to watch: slow interactive responses, token-cost spike, regressed hallucination on saved prompt set.
- Immediate seller script (30s): "We’re taking a short step to stabilize your experience. I’ll share exact details and a timeline within an hour."
- 3 immediate SE commands (console/API):
  * snapshot-metrics --route <route> --since 5m
  * toggle-routing-policy --route <route> --variant <cached|lite-quant>
  * set-pilot-cap --customer <id> --max-tokens 256
- Escalation path: SE -> Platform on-call -> SRE escalation if not stabilized in 10m.

Handoff script (Slack copy/paste)
"Incident: sales-surgeon <customer-name> <short> — P95>3s. Route: <id>. Model: <id>. Last deploy: <deploy-id> @ <time>. Actions tried: rerouted -> lite-quant (timestamp), cap tokens to 256 (timestamp). Need platform to (1) check GPU pool saturation (2) consider rollback of deploy <id> or increase priority. Traces: <trace-ids>."

Runbook snippets (for Ops)
- How to pin a route: UI path + API sample
- How to rollback model: reference to standard rollback playbook PR-ops-rollback.md
- Quick cost check: token spend delta and projected 24h burn if current rate continues

Customer scenarios (short vignettes)
- Fintech: pilot chat returns correct but slow for compliance workflow — immediate action: degrade to cached-variant and reduce streaming to prioritize throughput. Call out compliance: confirm that cached variant still respects PII handling policies.
- Marketplace: bursty traffic during promotion causing queue growth — immediate action: apply token caps on non-critical endpoints, enable autoscale burst for 30m if contract permits.

Metrics & guardrails to communicate to customers
- Baseline SLOs for pilots: P95 < 1.2s (interactive UI), token cost per session < $0.50 per 1k tokens (pilot target), availability 99.5%
- Communicate that short mitigations may change answer length, not semantics.

Open questions (for doc iteration)
- Exact console/API commands to include for non-ops SEs (TODO: add copy/paste snippets)
- Who owns making the consumer-facing language template final? (PM or CSM?)
- Need a playbook variant for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) with different escalation contacts.

Next steps (how this doc should evolve)
- Convert to a 2-slide seller-facing quick card + 1-page SE runbook with copy/paste commands (by 2026-03-01)
- Add screenshots and exact CLI/SDK snippets (by 2026-03-10)
- Validate with two live pilot accounts in March sprint and iterate language based on feedback (owner: Priya Nair)

Notes to self / rough edits to keep in later versions:
- Add a short "what not to do" list (no unscheduled model swaps, avoid swapping to a non-compatible architecture that changes logits semantics)
- Include sample telemetry dashboards that should be checked first (latency heatmap, pool utilization, route timeline)
- Consider a condensed one-row cheat card for AE mobile use

End of sketch.

Attachments to add in final: example Slack incident, console screenshots, sample API calls (toggle-routing-policy, set-pilot-cap, snapshot-metrics), link to ops rollback playbook.

Last edited notes:
- SE feedback 2026-02-10: add clearer distinction between "degrade" (same model family, different quant/profile) and "swap" (different model weights).
- Platform note 2026-02-12: need a non-admin path for SEs to toggle pilot caps safely (work in progress).
